correctness.rationale: For B of size 2k+1 and a Sym(A)-invariant relation R on A^k, reflexivity and symmetry transfer from any pair of tuples using at most 2k atoms. The nontrivial transitivity lifting uses finite quotient Q=B^k/E. For stabilizers K containing pointwise fixers of ≤k atoms, graph connectivity of transpositions outside two supports S,T (since B>S∪T) implies the intersection fixer is in K. Minimal support S is K-setwise-invariant, giving coset orbits Inj_t(B)/H with t≤k. On each equality-pattern orbit the quotient map selects an equivariant injective list of input coordinates modulo H; the same finite presentation defines a quotient map over arbitrary A, whose kernel agrees with R by supportwise injection of any input pair into B. The sharp counterexample relates equal or disjoint supports of injective k-tuples: on 2k atoms disjointness is complementation, a genuine equivalence; on 2k+1 atoms chains via disjoint k-sets break transitivity. Argument treats repeated tuples as singleton classes, infinite A and k≥2, and does not assume definability.
residual_risks: No mechanized formal proof of finite quotient presentation; no claim for arbitrary atom structures beyond Sym(A).
